props.heading: Property is our full-time business, not a side affair
props.body:
Prudent Realty was founded in 2014 by two engineers who could not find a straightforward property consultant when buying their first home. Twelve years later, we have closed over 500 deals across the residential and commercial markets of Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

We are a RERA-registered agency (RERA Reg. No. MAHARERA-A-12345678 / TN-RERA-2024-P-87654321). Every property we list is verified for clear title, approved building plan and occupancy certificate before it reaches a buyer.

We do not chase volume. We take on a limited number of clients at a time so each one gets the same attention — from the first site visit through to loan closure and registration.

props.label: Home Buyer Guide
props.heading: Common questions about buying, selling and renting

items.q: What is RERA and why does it matter?
items.a: RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Authority) is a government-mandated registration that every residential project must obtain before it can advertise or sell units. A RERA-registered project means the developer has disclosed the approved plans, timeline and carpet area to the authority. We only work with RERA-registered projects. You can verify any project's registration at maharera.mahaonline.gov.in or the respective state RERA website.

items.q: What are the stages of buying a property?
items.a: Generally: 1) Budget assessment and home loan pre-qualification — we can connect you with lenders to know your eligibility before you start looking. 2) Property shortlisting and site visits — we accompany you to every visit. 3) Booking and token amount — usually 5-10% of the property value. 4) Legal due diligence — title check, encumbrance, approved plan verification. 5) Home loan processing and sanction. 6) Sale deed execution and registration at the sub-registrar's office. 7) Possession and handover.

items.q: How much does stamp duty and registration cost?
items.a: Stamp duty rates vary by state. In Maharashtra, stamp duty is approximately 5-6% of the property value (with a 1% rebate for women buyers). Registration fee is 1% of the property value (capped at ₹30,000 for most properties). In Tamil Nadu, stamp duty is 7% and registration 4%. In Karnataka, stamp duty is 5-6% and registration 1%. Our team provides a precise cost sheet for any property you are considering.

items.q: What documents do I need for a home loan?
items.a: Typically: PAN Card, Aadhaar Card, last 3 years' IT returns, last 6 months' bank statements, salary slips (for salaried) or CA-certified financials (for self-employed), property documents once shortlisted. Most lenders approve pre-qualified amounts within 5-7 working days. We help prepare the full application package.

items.q: Do you charge the buyer or the seller?
items.a: Our brokerage is paid by the party we represent. For a buyer, we are typically paid by the developer or seller. For a seller listing with us, our commission is agreed upfront in writing and is only payable on successful closing. There are no hidden charges. Our fee structure is shared before any work begins.

items.q: How do I list my property with you?
items.a: Call or WhatsApp us with the property address and basic details. We will schedule a visit, take photographs, verify the documents, and do a market-rate valuation. If you choose to proceed, we sign an exclusive or non-exclusive listing agreement, and your property goes live within 48 hours with professional photos and a detailed description.

items.q: What should I check before buying a resale flat?
items.a: Key checks: clear title and chain of ownership, encumbrance certificate for the last 13 years, approved building plan and completion certificate, occupancy certificate (OC), no-objection certificates (NOC) from the fire department and pollution board for high-rises, and the society's current maintenance charges and corpus fund status. Our legal team does all of these checks before we recommend any resale property.

items.q: Is NRIs buying property in India?
items.a: Yes, NRIs (including OCI cardholders) can buy residential and commercial property in India without special permission. Agricultural land, plantation land and farmhouses require RBI/FEMA approval. Home loans are available to NRIs from most Indian banks. All documents can be handled remotely through a power of attorney. We have helped over 40 NRI families buy property from the US, UK, Canada, UAE and Singapore.

posts.title: Maharashtra Budget 2026: What home buyers should know
posts.excerpt: The Maharashtra state budget has reduced stamp duty by 0.5% for properties up to ₹75 lakh, and increased the ready-reckoner rate freeze for another year. Here is what it means for your purchase.
posts.body:
The Maharashtra state budget for 2026-27 brings several changes relevant to home buyers:

1. Stamp duty reduction: A 0.5% reduction in stamp duty for properties valued up to ₹75 lakh brings the effective rate to 4% for men and 3% for women (with the existing 1% rebate for women intact). A property of ₹70 lakh now saves approximately ₹35,000 in stamp duty.

2. Ready-reckoner rates: The government has frozen ready-reckoner rates for the fourth consecutive year — meaning circle rates stay at 2023 levels. For buyers, this means the minimum valuation on which stamp duty is calculated does not increase.

3. PMAY subsidy: The Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana continues for EWS/LIG categories, providing interest subsidy of up to ₹2.67 lakh on home loans.

As always, we recommend consulting a tax professional to understand how these changes apply to your specific situation.
